title: Companies Act, 2013 — Sections 241 and 242 (Oppression and mismanagement)

content.overview: Members who meet the threshold may apply to the Tribunal where the company's affairs are conducted in a manner prejudicial to the public interest or oppressive to members, or where a material change is likely to cause that result. The Tribunal may make any order it thinks fit to bring an end to the matters complained of.
content.glance: Members who meet the threshold may apply to the Tribunal where the company's affairs are conducted in a manner prejudicial to the public interest or oppressive to members, or where a material change is likely to cause that result. The Tribunal may make any order it thinks fit to bring an end to the matters complained of.
content.study: The threshold is in section 244: one hundred members or one-tenth of the members, or members holding one-tenth of the issued share capital, with a waiver power. Relief can regulate future conduct, set aside transactions, terminate or modify agreements, remove directors, or provide for purchase of shares. A mere loss of confidence is not enough. Just and equitable winding up is a separate ground under section 271.
